verses.text: Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of King Jehoshaphat's reign over Judah. He ruled for twelve years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, though he didn't go as far as his father and mother. He removed the sacred pillar his father had made for Baal.
Still, he clung to the sins Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel into, and he never gave them up.
Mesha king of Moab bred sheep. He supplied the king of Israel with a hundred thousand lambs and the wool from a hundred thousand rams.
After Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
King Jehoram left Samaria and called up all Israel's troops.

He sent word to King Jehoshaphat of Judah: “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you come with me to fight Moab?” Jehoshaphat replied, “I'll go with you. My people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”
“Which way should we go?” he asked. Jehoram answered, “Through the wilderness of Edom.”
The kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom marched together, taking a roundabout route for seven days. They ran out of water for the troops and the animals traveling with them.
The king of Israel said, “We're in trouble! The LORD has brought these three kings together to hand them over to Moab.”

But Jehoshaphat asked, “Isn't there a prophet of the LORD here so we can ask the LORD what to do?” One of the king of Israel's servants answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on Elijah's hands.”
Jehoshaphat said, “The LORD's word is with him.” So the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom went down to see him.

Elisha asked the king of Israel, “What business do I have with you? Go to your father's prophets and your mother's prophets.” The king of Israel answered, “No. The LORD has brought these three kings together to hand them over to Moab.”
Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD of Armies lives, whom I serve, if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat of Judah, I wouldn't even look at you or give you a hearing.
Now bring me a musician.” While the musician played, the LORD's hand came on Elisha.
He said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Dig trenches all through this valley.’
The LORD says, ‘You won't see wind or rain, but this valley will fill with water, and you, your livestock, and your other animals will drink.
This is easy for the LORD. He'll also hand Moab over to you.
You'll strike every fortified town and every good town. You'll cut down every good tree, plug every spring, and ruin every good field with stones.’”
The next morning, around the time of the offering, water came flowing from the direction of Edom and covered the land.
When the Moabites heard the kings had come to fight them, they assembled everyone old enough to put on armor and took their stand at the border.
They got up early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water. From where they stood, the water looked as red as blood.
“That's blood,” they said. “The kings must have turned on one another and killed each other. Come on, Moab! Let's take the plunder!”
When they reached Israel's camp, the Israelites rose up and attacked the Moabites, who fled from them. The Israelites pressed into Moab, striking them down as they went.

They tore down the towns. Each man threw a stone onto each good field until the fields were covered. They plugged all the springs and chopped down all the good trees. Only the stones of Kir Hareseth were left standing, and the men with slings surrounded it and attacked it.
When the king of Moab saw he was losing the battle, he took seven hundred swordsmen and tried to break through to the king of Edom. They couldn't get through.

Then he took his oldest son, who would have been king after him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. Great wrath came against Israel, so the Israelites withdrew and went back to their own land.
